policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 19 Jan close (1x4 3.82, 3x6 3.53, 6x9 3.38, 9x12 3.38 vs WIBOR 3M 3.94) price roughly 55bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The MPC held at 4.00% on 14 Jan. Glapiński (15 Jan): a terminal rate of about 3.5% with a real rate of at least 1-1.5%, cuts in 25bp steps; he excluded neither February nor March (or even April). Kotecki (16 Jan) expects the MPC to resume cuts in February and PKO now sees February as highly probable; Wnorowski (16 Jan) prefers March; core CPI 2.7% in December (16 Jan; 2.8% expected). Tyrowicz (19 Jan): 'rather no room' to cut; Credit Agricole and Deutsche Bank expect March (DB: March and May, to 3.50%).
policy.risk_text: February is now debated inside the MPC (Kotecki for; Wnorowski, Tyrowicz against): if the cut slips beyond March the front-end roll-down does not materialise, and global long-end volatility (tariffs, Fed independence) hits the 10Y through the asset swap.

cpi.m: Dec final (GUS, 15 Jan); Nov 2.5%; Dec core 2.7% (NBP, 16 Jan)

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 CPI 2.4% y/y (final). The March 2026 projection is due with the March MPC meeting.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP; 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; FinMin Domański (16 Jan): the 2025 central-budget deficit came in a dozen-plus billion below the PLN 288.8bn limit; the President signed the 2026 budget on 19 Jan and referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal for follow-up review (the act is in force).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions; 2026 needs ~26% financed (12 Jan); Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% and held on 14 Jan; December CPI 2.4% y/y (final, 15 Jan), core 2.7%; the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters 2.6%); the March projection is the next policy gate. GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3; IMF (19 Jan) raised Poland's 2026 growth forecast to 3.5%. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 19 Jan: EU weighed EUR 93bn of counter-tariffs over Greenland; euro-area December HICP was revised to 1.9%; China Q4 GDP 4.5%. POLGB yields rose 1-8bp (PKO). The President signed and referred the budget (evening).

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance; January sales 9 Jan (done: PLN 13.7bn incl. additional sale), 22 Jan (plan 8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); EUR 3.25bn priced on 8 Jan. 16 Jan: 36-week T-bills PLN 3.8bn at 3.645%.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (22 and 28 Jan) rather than the day before. The 9 Jan auction cleared PLN 13.7bn with 1.86x cover. For the front end the 3-4 Feb MPC is the next event: February is debated after Glapiński's dovish conference; the March projection decides the cut timing.

core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% with ~55bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00% (a hike is the next move in market pricing), the Fed is on hold into June, the BoE eases gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. (Erste's CDS/spread table for 19 Jan looked stale or inconsistent, so it is not quoted.) The EU weighed EUR 93bn of counter-tariffs (19 Jan).
